dialog.body: Good morning, Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hey, good morning. Yeah, I'm calling about the storm drain on Howard Street. Again. This is like the third time somebody from this house has called you guys about the same drain.
Okay. Let me get the address first so I can pull up what we have. What's the address?

Thirty-one Howard Street. Down in the Fifth Ward. If you're coming from Thames you go past, um, where the bank used to be, the one that's empty now, and you turn there, and it's on the left before the corner. The drain's right at the corner.
Thirty-one Howard Street. Okay. And your name?
Ivan Duarte. D-U-A-R-T-E. I rent the second-floor apartment. The house is Priya Okafor's, she's my landlord, she's the one who called back in January.

Ivan Duarte, D-U-A-R-T-E, second-floor apartment at thirty-one Howard. Give me one second, I'm pulling it up. [pause] Okay, yes, I see it. There's a call from Mrs. Okafor on January twelfth, and then another one February twenty-third from, is it Min-jun Okafor?
Yeah, that's her son. So you've got it all right there. Then you know.
I see the history, yes. So tell me what happened this time. This was with the rain over the weekend?

Yeah, the rain Friday into Saturday. Same thing. The drain at the corner backs up, the water comes up out of the grate, and the whole street ponds. It was over the curb, right up to the top step. Like you could not walk out the front door without boots up to your knees.
Okay. So the drain backed up and the street ponded over the curb, up to the top step of the house.

Right. And I'm telling you, it's the same every time. It comes up out of the street drain first. That's always first. And then it comes for the house. That's how it went in January, that's how it went last month. So this time I didn't wait. Saturday morning I was out there sandbagging the door before it even got bad.
You put sandbags at the door.

Yeah. Me and, well, me mostly. I'm upstairs, I don't even use the basement, but it's not like I'm gonna just watch it. And it held. Basement's dry. Thank God, honestly, because they already got it twice this winter. Once after that big storm in January and then again after the nor'easter end of February. Twice. And the second time was way worse, it was like eight inches down there.
Okay, so I want to make sure I have this right for the file. The basement stayed dry this time, nothing got in.
Nothing got in this time. Because of the sandbags. Not because anything got fixed.
Understood. And the two floods before were the January storm and the late-February nor'easter. Those are both already in here.

Yeah. And see, that's my point. It's all in there. You guys came in January, the day after she called, and what they did, they cleared leaves off the grate. That's it. Scooped the leaves off the top and left. Nothing underneath. And then it flooded again in February, eight inches, and then you guys came and jetted the line and found it was partly blocked. Partly blocked! So it was blocked the whole time, back in January too, probably.
I see the note from February twenty-fifth, yes. The crew jetted the line under the corner.

Right, and then a supervisor called Min-jun back that Thursday and said, oh, there's a bigger fix being looked at. No date. Nothing. That was two weeks ago. And then it rains for a day and a half and we're right back out there with sandbags. Like, what are we supposed to do every time it rains? I can't be home every storm. I work. If this happens on a shift, who's sandbagging?
No, I hear you. That's a lot to be dealing with every time it rains.

It is. And no offense to you, you're just answering the phone, but every time it's, okay, we logged it, okay, we'll send somebody. And somebody comes and does a little something and it doesn't fix it.

So what I can do, I'm adding this weekend's backup to the same file. It's flagged as a repeat backup already, from February, so this goes right in with it. The street ponding over the curb up to the top step, the drain backing up first, and that you sandbagged and the basement stayed dry. And I'll make sure the supervisor sees it today.
Okay, but see, that's what I want. I want the supervisor to actually call. Me. Not, like, leave a note in the file. I want somebody who can tell me what this bigger fix is and when it's happening.
Sure. You want a callback from a supervisor.
Yes. Please.
Okay. What's the best number to reach you?

Four oh one, five five five, oh one six nine. That's my cell. And sorry if I sound weird, I'm out in the shed in the back yard right now. It's kind of my office, I got a little desk out here, it's the only place I can hear myself think. Signal's [inaudible] sometimes.
You cut out a little there. I've got four oh one, five five five, oh one six nine. Is that right?
Yeah, that's right. Oh one six nine.

Okay. Four oh one, five five five, oh one six nine, Ivan Duarte, callback requested from a supervisor about the repeat backup at the corner by thirty-one Howard. Is there a time that's better for you?

Honestly any time. If I don't pick up I'm probably on the floor at work, just leave a message and I'll call back. But I want it to be somebody who knows about the bigger fix. Not just, we're looking into it.
I'll put that in the note, that you're asking specifically about the status of the larger repair and a timeline.
Thank you. Can you tell me, like, is there anything on there? Like a date for that? Anything at all?

I don't see a date on my end. All it says is what you told me, that the supervisor spoke with Min-jun on the twenty-sixth and a larger fix is under review. That's as far as my screen goes. The supervisor would have more than I do, which is why I want them calling you.

Yeah. Okay. I figured. [pause] It's just, it's March. We got a whole spring of rain coming. And the landlord, she's been here thirty-something years, she's not, like, she shouldn't have to be hauling stuff out of that basement every month. She already lost a bunch of stuff in January.
I understand. And is anybody sending a crew out this time, is that something you want? Is the drain still backed up now, or did it go down?

It went down. Took most of Saturday but it went down. The street's fine now. There's like a mud line on the sidewalk by the corner, that's it. So I don't need somebody to come scoop leaves, if that's what you mean. I need the actual thing fixed.

Okay. So no standing water right now, it drained off by Saturday. I'll note that too. I'm not booking a separate crew visit, I'm sending it up with the callback request so the supervisor's looking at the whole picture.
Okay. Fine. That's what I want.

Let me read it back so you know what's going in. Thirty-one Howard Street, Fifth Ward. Caller Ivan Duarte, tenant, second-floor apartment. Early-March rain, Friday into Saturday, the corner drain backed up, water came up out of the drain and ponded over the curb up to the top step. Caller sandbagged the door, basement stayed dry. Basement previously flooded twice this winter, January storm and late-February nor'easter, both on file. Requests supervisor callback on the larger repair and a timeline, at four oh one, five five five, oh one six nine. Does that cover it?
Yeah. That's it. That's everything.
Okay. It's in. I'm walking it over to the supervisor's desk this morning myself.
All right. I appreciate that, Lorraine. Really. I'm not trying to yell at you. It's just, we keep calling and it keeps happening, you know?
I know. You're not yelling. You've got every reason to keep calling.
Yeah, well. Hopefully I don't have to call again. Hopefully somebody calls me.
That's the plan. You have a good rest of your Monday, Ivan.
Yeah, you too. Thanks.
